t: Here at the corner of Oxford Street and Tottenham Court Road, the Oxford Music Hall once stood. Charles Morton established it in 1861 on the site of a pub called the Boar and Castle. Morton had built the first purpose-built tavern music hall, the Canterbury, and became known as the Father of the Halls. The architect was Finch Hill, a Victorian theatre and music hall specialist. In 1917 it became a theatre, and in 1921 the New Oxford Theatre. It closed in May 1926 and was demolished.
